title: Maybank Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Maybank Marathon 2026 Review: Hills, Heat, Cut-offs, Toilets
meta_description: Maybank Marathon 2026 review: a 4.20am start in 25°C with a breeze, village roads with climbs, a seven-hour limit, a 2:16 winner, and runners' complaints about toilets and water.
dek: What it was like to run the 15th Maybank Marathon in Gianyar, Bali, on 23 August 2026: the rolling village course, the weather from the 4.20am start, the cut-offs, the crowds, what runners complained about, and how fast the field was.
verdict: Enter if you want a big Elite Label marathon with village crowds and can race on a rolling course. In 2026, 14,100 runners from 46 countries took part; the marathon started at 4.20am in 25°C air with a dew point of 23°C and a 7-9 knot breeze, and the limit is seven hours. The catch is the climbs and the basics. Indonesia's 2025 national women's winner called km 8 to 34 full of climbs, and in 2026 marathoners said there were no portable toilets on the course and little cold water. Train on hills, carry electrolyte if you rely on it, and aim to finish before it passed 29°C at 9.30am.

sections.heading: The Course: Village Roads, Rice Fields and Repeated Climbs
paragraphs: The race starts and finishes at Bali United Training Center in Gianyar [1]. The course begins on the Bypass I.B. Mantra, an arterial road, and then turns through the villages and rice fields of Gianyar regency [2]. The roads closed for it run through the districts of Gianyar, Blahbatuh and Sukawati, including Jalan Pantai Lebih, Pantai Masceti and Pantai Saba, and roads through Tulikup, Bona and Pering [3], and the route passes the town square in Gianyar [4].

It is not flat. A kumparan reporter who ran the 10 km described several challenging climbs [2]. After the 2025 race, Indonesia's national women's marathon winner, Odekta Naibaho, said the stretch from 8 km to 34 km was full of climbs, and that year's men's winner called the course really difficult; the organiser said the course had again been certified by AIMS and World Athletics [5].

The crowds are the thing runners mention most. Schoolchildren, residents in traditional dress and dancers with gamelan lined parts of the route [2]. Febry Arnold, an Indonesian runner based in San Francisco who was running an 86th marathon, said small children were up at 4am to cheer and that no other marathon had dancers out along the whole route [6].

sections.heading: The Weather: Warm, but With a Breeze
paragraphs: Ngurah Rai airport, about 20 km south-west of the start, recorded 25°C at the 4.20am marathon start, with a dew point of 23°C, 89% humidity and a 7 to 9 knot wind [7]. It stayed at 25°C until 7am, while the dew point dropped to 22°C [7].

It then warmed steadily: 27°C at 8am, 29°C by 9.30am and 30°C by 11am, with the breeze holding at 8 to 10 knots [7]. On the results, the middle marathoner crossed the line about 5 hours 28 minutes after the gun [8], at around 9.50am, when the airport read 29°C [7].
The organiser can cancel the race for heavy rain or lightning, and does not refund entries if it does [9].

sections.heading: Cut-offs, Aid and Toilets
paragraphs: The limits are seven hours for the marathon, three and a half hours for the half and two hours for the 10 km, and anyone finishing outside them gets no medal; only marathon finishers get a finisher shirt [9]. The organiser can also set checkpoints on the course, and runners who miss one are put on transport to the finish [9]. Race time is counted from the gun [9]. The results still list runners who crossed late: 65 marathoners, 251 half marathoners and 62 10 km runners finished after the limit on gun time [8].

Runners disagreed about the aid. The kumparan reporter in the 10 km found a water station at every kilometre [2]. But marathoners told detikBali that the only cold water was at a single station, and another runner said the isotonic and water stations were far apart [4].

Toilets were the main complaint. A marathoner from Lombok said runners used petrol stations and residents' homes and queued for them, and said there were no portable toilets on the course, unlike in earlier years [4]. A half marathoner from Toraja said the toilet signs were clear and that the portable toilets were at the venue [4]. The organiser said it would evaluate the basic facilities for next year [4].

sections.heading: Roads and Race Morning
paragraphs: The main closure was the northbound side of the Bypass I.B. Mantra, from Simpang Ketewel to Simpang Tegal Besar, from midnight to 2pm on race day, and the village roads on the route were closed from 3am to noon [3]. On the Saturday evening part of the bypass was closed from 7pm and traffic ran two-way on the other side [3].

Residents along the route were asked to tie up or cage their dogs and cats for the weekend, so that they would not chase runners [3]. The venue was already filling up with runners from 3am [2]. A marathoner said the cheering teams only appeared from about 6am [4], so, by that account, the first hour and 40 minutes of the marathon had little organised support.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The front is very fast. Kenya's Michael Kimani Kamau won in 2:16:10 and Veronicah Njeri Maina in 2:37:22, each taking Rp260 million [1][10]. Nine men broke 2:21 [8]. The organiser brought in 11 elite runners from Kenya and Ethiopia [11].

Behind the invited elites the field drops away. Tenth place in the marathon was Robi Syianturi, the national winner, in 2:28:30, and tenth woman was the national winner Ina Lydia in 3:09:55 [8]; each took Rp100 million in the national category [1]. The national men's race was decided by one second, 2:28:30 to 2:28:31 [8].

In the half marathon, tenth place was 1:11:39 for men and 1:31:49 for women, and the 10 km was won by Daniel Simanjuntak in 30:54 [8]. The middle finisher in the half took about 2:44 on the gun and in the 10 km about 1:29 [8]. Most of the field is Indonesian: nearly one in ten runners came from abroad [10].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Entry is by ballot. In 2026 Maybank customers had a pre-sale from 9 to 30 January and the public ballot ran from 9 to 22 February; the marathon cost Rp950,000 for Indonesians and Rp1.6 million for foreigners, the half Rp800,000 or Rp1 million and the 10 km Rp650,000 or Rp800,000 [12]. Fees are not refunded, and entries cannot be transferred or sold [9].

Race packs were collected at the venue on 21 and 22 August [12], in person only, with the confirmation email and identity card [9]. The minimum age is 18 for the marathon, 17 for the half and 15 for the 10 km [9].

The venue is busy after the race. Maybank Indonesia's president director said the Adidas stand ran out of stock in less than a day, with long queues [4]. The field grew by about 500 from 2025 [6], to 14,100, and the organiser is studying whether to spread the 2027 event over two days [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a big, well-supported Elite Label marathon with a holiday attached, can run hills, and like crowds: the village support is what runners remember. It also works as a first overseas race; a Taiwanese runner on a first race abroad finished the half inside the limit and was moved by the children cheering [6].
Think twice if you want a flat course or a personal best, or if you need regular toilets and cold drinks on the course. In 2026 runners found both short [4].
The 2027 date, fees and format had not been published when this was written. The organiser was reviewing a two-day format [1], and AIMS listed no 2027 date [13].

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's rules, the full results, airport weather records, Indonesian and English-language reporting, and runners' accounts given to reporters.

faqs.question: What time does the Maybank Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Before dawn. In 2026 the marathon started at 4.20am, the half marathon at 5.30am, the 10 km at 6am and the wheelchair race at 6.10am, all from Bali United Training Center in Gianyar. Runners were filling the venue from 3am. The 2027 schedule had not been published, and a two-day format is under review.

faqs.question: Is the Maybank Marathon course hilly?
faqs.answer: Yes, it rolls. The 2026 route ran from the Bypass I.B. Mantra into Gianyar's villages and rice fields, and a reporter who ran the 10 km described several challenging climbs. After the 2025 race, the national women's winner said the stretch from 8 km to 34 km was full of climbs.

faqs.question: How hot is the Maybank Marathon?
faqs.answer: Warm and humid, with a breeze. At the 4.20am start in 2026, Ngurah Rai airport recorded 25°C, a dew point of 23°C, 89% humidity and a 7 to 9 knot wind. It stayed at 25°C until 7am, then reached 27°C at 8am, 29°C by 9.30am and 30°C by 11am.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Maybank Marathon?
faqs.answer: Seven hours for the marathon, three and a half hours for the half marathon and two hours for the 10 km, timed from the gun. Runners outside the limit get no medal, and only marathon finishers get a finisher shirt. Runners who miss an on-course checkpoint are taken to the finish.

faqs.question: Are there toilets on the Maybank Marathon course?
faqs.answer: Few portable ones in 2026. Marathoners told detikBali they saw no portable toilets on the course and used petrol stations and residents' homes, queuing for them. Signs pointed to the homes, and portable toilets were at the venue. The organiser said it would evaluate the facilities for the next race.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 about the 15th edition, run on 23 August 2026. Weather is from Ngurah Rai airport METAR observations, not a forecast. Results counts are from the official results pages (sorted by gun time); the organiser's 14,100 participants differ from the 11,589 names listed in the three races. The official 2026 race guide is a flipbook that could not be read, so the route map, aid-station list and intermediate cut-off times are not given. Tempo's English report calls Isania Tarigan the national marathon runner-up; the results show the runner in the half marathon, which is used. Runners in the complaints report are not named in the body. ANTARA was not used. No rating.
